law: Commutativity in a symmetric monoidal category: σ ∘ (f ⊗ g) = g ⊗ f.
name: comm_add

law: Hadamard product is commutative (SMC symmetry).
name: comm_mul

law: Associativity of sequential composition in a category.
name: assoc_add

law: Associativity of parallel composition in a monoidal category.
name: assoc_mul

law: Additive identity: a + 0 = a.
name: id_add

law: Multiplicative identity: a * 1 = a.
name: id_mul

law: Double negation: ¬¬a = a (involution).
name: double_neg

law: Subtraction as addition of inverse: a - b = a + (-b).
name: sub_to_add

law: SiLU definition: silu(x) = x · σ(x).
name: silu_expand

law: The manual-silu fold: x · σ(x) = silu(x) — the definitional inverse of silu_expand, and the mediating 3-cell of the silu_expand/silu_mul_form × swiglu_fuse critical pairs.
name: silu_fold

law: SwiGLU: silu(g)*u = (g*sigmoid(g))*u (factor for prefix sharing).
name: silu_mul_form

law: x / (|x| + 1) = softsign(x) — the bounded rational map, written as a three-op decomposed spelling, folds into the one kernel.
name: softsign_fold

law: Self-composition: x² = x · x.
name: square_expand

law: pow(x, 2) ≡ square(x) ≡ x·x (SwiGLU/RMSNorm bridge).
name: pow_to_square

law: Reverse: square(x) ≡ pow(x, 2) for shape/cost reasons.
name: square_to_pow

law: x·x = square(x): the mul spelling of x² folds to the unary kernel — the definitional inverse of square_expand.
name: mul_square

law: mul commutes with select: sel(u) ⊙ sel(v) = sel(u ⊙ v) — the elementwise product of two slices is the slice of the product (naturality of the elementwise action over the select view).  Removes one dispatched op per site.
name: select_mul

law: A transpose whose swap axes coincide (d0 == d1 mod rank) or whose swapped extents are both 1 is a semantic no-op — the stride permutation maps each position to itself; strip the view.
name: transpose_noop

law: chunk(u, chunks=1, dim, index) is u — a one-section partition returns the whole tensor unchanged.
name: chunk_single

law: unsqueeze(u, d) · v = u · v when the inserted axis is a broadcast pad and the broadcast grids coincide — the lifted operand reads the same positions, so the pad view is dead.  Drops one dispatched op per site (the exported ALiBi spelling carries it).
name: mul_unsq_pad_l

law: Right-operand twin of mul_unsq_pad_l: u · unsqueeze(v, d) = u · v under the same broadcast-pad grid guard.
name: mul_unsq_pad_r

law: unsqueeze(u, d) - v = u - v under the broadcast-pad guard — same strip for the asymmetric operand pair (the guard, not the op's commutativity, is what carries it).
name: sub_unsq_pad_l

law: u + unsqueeze(v, d) = u + v under the broadcast-pad grid guard — the add sibling of mul_unsq_pad_r: the lifted operand's pad view is dead when the broadcast grids coincide.  Minted by auto-cond from the intake census's ``mixed:add_unsqueeze_r_id`` candidate and admitted off a strictly-real paying site (``RelativePositionBias`` — see docs/results_realcorpus.md).
name: add_unsq_pad_r

law: unsqueeze(u, d) · unsqueeze(v, d) = unsqueeze(u · v, d) — elementwise mul commutes with a shared size-1 axis insertion exactly when the broadcast grids coincide AND both operands' flat-read maps agree across the two orders (the flat-map-unsq region — equal ranks always qualify; unequal ranks only when the insert lands in the pad).  Fuses two views into one and shrinks the pointwise domain a rank.
name: mul_unsq_nat

law: reshape(u, S) · v = u · v when the reshape is broadcast-inert — equal broadcast grids force the reshape to a 1-axis insert/remove (a permuting reshape changes an extent and the grids disagree).  Grid equality is the minted single-clause guard.
name: mul_reshape_inert_l

law: exp(u) / Σ exp(u) = softmax(u): the manual normalization fold — a composed-then-reduced chain IS the kernel's definition.  Folds div+exp+sum to one dispatched op.
name: softmax_fold

law: chunk-half · σ(chunk-half) IS glu(u): the manual-GLU fold — a ⊗ σ(b) over the two equal halves of u IS the kernel's definition.  Folds mul+sigmoid+2 chunks to one dispatched op.
name: glu_fold

law: x·rsqrt(mean(x²)+eps)·w IS rms_norm(x, w): the manual-RMSNorm fold — composed-then-reduced then scaled IS the kernel's definition.  Folds mul+mul+rsqrt+add+mean+pow to one dispatched op.
name: rms_norm_fold

law: x·rsqrt(mean(x²)+eps) IS rms_norm(x): the weight-free manual-RMSNorm fold — the gained fold's inner ``mul`` and a real spelling of its own (gain-free RMSNorm blocks).
name: rms_norm_fold_nogain

law: 1 / sqrt(x) = rsqrt(x): the two-op reciprocal-root spelling folds to the dispatched kernel — the canonical form the RMSNorm fold's pattern pins.
name: div_sqrt_to_rsqrt

law: pow(x, -0.5) = rsqrt(x): the negative-half-power spelling folds to the dispatched kernel — the same canonicalization as div_sqrt_to_rsqrt one op-family over.
name: pow_to_rsqrt

law: reciprocal(sqrt(x)) = rsqrt(x): the exported ``1/sqrt`` spelling — aten lowers scalar-over-tensor div to reciprocal — folds to the same canonical kernel.
name: recip_sqrt_to_rsqrt

law: (a/b)·c = (a·c)/b — pointwise div/mul naturality, exact for any broadcast (the decay-weighted score's scale slides out of the product).
name: mul_div_swap

law: (a/c)@v = (a@v)/c when c is scalar — linear readout of a scalar-denominated operand; the score scale exits the contraction.
name: matmul_div_distribute

law: x/c + y/c = (x+y)/c — shared-denominator factoring over the additive monoid; the score scale exits the block sum the way it exited the contraction.
name: div_add_factor

law: Distributivity of linear maps over addition (bilinearity).
name: distribute_matmul_over_add

law: Factoring common linear maps (reverse distributivity).
name: factor_matmul

law: Merge shared-input projections: x@W1 + x@W2 = x@(W1+W2).
name: weight_factor_matmul

law: Reverse weight merge (lets eqsat weigh fused vs split forms).
name: weight_distribute_matmul

law: Merge shared-input nn.Linears: linear(x,W1)+linear(x,W2) = linear(x, W1+W2)  (transpose distributes over +).
name: weight_factor_linear

law: Expand a merged nn.Linear so eqsat can compare both forms.
name: weight_distribute_linear

law: Bilinearity: linear maps distribute over addition in BOTH slots.
name: right_distribute_matmul

law: Factor a shared right-weight (the slot `x @ W` uses).
name: right_factor_matmul

law: Factor a shared right-hand nn.Linear weight.
name: right_factor_linear

law: Compose stacked nn.Linears: fused weight is B @ A (transposes flip the product order).
name: assoc_linear

law: Reverse linear composition: linear(x, B@A) = linear(linear(x, A), B) (eqsat weighs fused vs split).
name: assoc_linear_rev

law: Affine-map composition: (B,b2)∘(A,b1) = (BA, B·b1 + b2).  Fused weight is B @ A (same transpose flip as assoc_linear); the fused bias is spelled linear(x, BA, B·b1) + b2 so both B-products fold at compile time — one GEMM plus one broadcast add at runtime.
name: assoc_linear_bias

law: Reverse affine composition (eqsat weighs fused vs split).
name: assoc_linear_bias_rev

law: Naturality: scalar multiplication commutes with linear maps.
name: naturality_scalar

law: Reverse naturality: pull scalar into the matmul's input.
name: naturality_scalar_rev

law: Associativity of composition in a category: (f∘g)∘h = f∘(g∘h).
name: assoc_matmul

law: Reverse associativity: f∘(g∘h) = (f∘g)∘h.
name: assoc_matmul_rev

law: split commutes with pointwise add when the other operand is scalar: the partition reads the same elementwise grid; the scalar accompanies every block unchanged.
name: split_scalar_add_r

law: split commutes with pointwise add when the other operand is scalar: the partition reads the same elementwise grid; the scalar accompanies every block unchanged.
name: split_scalar_add_l

law: split commutes with pointwise div when the other operand is scalar: the partition reads the same elementwise grid; the scalar accompanies every block unchanged.

law: split commutes with pointwise div when the other operand is scalar: the partition reads the same elementwise grid; the scalar accompanies every block unchanged.

law: split commutes with pointwise mul when the other operand is scalar: the partition reads the same elementwise grid; the scalar accompanies every block unchanged.
name: split_scalar_mul_r

law: split commutes with pointwise mul when the other operand is scalar: the partition reads the same elementwise grid; the scalar accompanies every block unchanged.
name: split_scalar_mul_l

law: split commutes with pointwise sub when the other operand is scalar: the partition reads the same elementwise grid; the scalar accompanies every block unchanged.
name: split_scalar_sub_r

law: split commutes with pointwise sub when the other operand is scalar: the partition reads the same elementwise grid; the scalar accompanies every block unchanged.
name: split_scalar_sub_l

law: Product universal property: <f,g> = (f x g) . Delta.  Two projections of the same input are ONE GEMM into V x V, then project.  (Fused SwiGLU gate/up — MergedColumnParallelLinear.)
name: swiglu_fuse

law: Pairing without a gate nonlinearity: mul(<pi1 f>, <pi2 g>) recovers the parallel-product form.
name: parallel_mul_fuse

law: Triple pairing <q,k,v> : X -> V^3 — three projections of the same input are ONE GEMM into the product space, then three zero-cost chunk projections.  (Fused QKV.)
name: qkv_fuse

law: Asymmetric triple pairing: the same product law as qkv_fuse, but the three projections have different output dims — one GEMM, three uneven split views.  (GQA fused QKV.)
name: qkv_fuse_asym

law: Channel scale is a right diagonal: (xD)W = x(DW).  Folds the norm's affine gain into the weight at compile time.
name: linear_channel_scale

law: Reverse channel-scale fold (eqsat compares both forms).
name: linear_channel_scale_rev

law: Row scale is a left diagonal: commutes through the linear map to the output (naturality of scalar action).
name: linear_row_scale

law: Reverse row-scale hoist (eqsat compares both forms).
name: linear_row_scale_rev

law: linear(x, W∘c) = c·linear(x, W) — a channel scale folded into the weight migrates through the linear map and re-emerges as a row scale on the output (channel_scale_rev then row_scale, fused into one premise-guarded step).
name: linear_channel_to_row_scale

law: The diagonal is natural: unsqueeze->expand->reshape copies each kv head r times (repeat_kv).  SDPA implements that copy inside the kernel via enable_gqa — pushing Delta into the consumer deletes the materialisation entirely.
name: gqa_absorb_repeat

law: softmax(qk^T s + m) v is sdpa — the additive mask is the kernel's attn_mask argument.
name: sdpa_fold_addmul

law: masked_fill(m, -inf) before softmax is a boolean attn_mask — logical_not turns the fill-mask into SDPA's keep-mask.

law: softmax(qk^T s + m) v is sdpa — the additive mask is the kernel's attn_mask argument.

law: masked_fill(m, -inf) before softmax is a boolean attn_mask — logical_not turns the fill-mask into SDPA's keep-mask.

law: softmax(qk^T s + m) v is sdpa — the additive mask is the kernel's attn_mask argument.

law: softmax(qk^T s + m) v is sdpa — the additive mask is the kernel's attn_mask argument.

name: sdpa_fold_masked_filldiv_drop

law: softmax(qk^T s + m) v is sdpa — the additive mask is the kernel's attn_mask argument.
name: sdpa_fold_add

law: masked_fill(m, -inf) before softmax is a boolean attn_mask — logical_not turns the fill-mask into SDPA's keep-mask.
name: sdpa_fold_masked_fill

law: softmax(qk^T s + m) v is sdpa — the additive mask is the kernel's attn_mask argument.

law: masked_fill(m, -inf) before softmax is a boolean attn_mask — logical_not turns the fill-mask into SDPA's keep-mask.
name: sdpa_fold_masked_fill_drop

law: softmax(q kᵀ) v is sdpa(q, k, v, scale=1) — the mask-free spelled attention is one fused kernel (the add/masked_fill family's empty-mask row).
name: sdpa_fold_nomask

law: softmax(q kᵀ / s) v is sdpa(q, k, v, scale=1/s) — the mask-free spelled form with the decomposed pre-softmax scale.
name: sdpa_fold_div_nomask

law: softmax(q kᵀ · s) v is sdpa(q, k, v, scale=s) — the mul spelling of the mask-free scaled fold, and the re-fusion half of the sdpa_expand pair (the mediating inverse for the expand/fold critical pair, the silu_fold analogue).
name: sdpa_fold_mul_nomask

law: unsq(u·v, d) = unsq(u, d)·unsq(v, d) — the size-1-axis insert distributes over elementwise mul: XLA's broadcast-sink direction, guarded to the flat-map-unsq region AND UD literal-in-range for both operand unsqs (the implicit-broadcast soundness envelope).
name: mul_unsq_rev

law: contiguous(x) is a value-identity relayout — the IR's semantics is value-level, so the strip is exact.
name: contiguous_id

law: clone(x) preserves values exactly — a materialization, not a value change.
name: clone_id

law: alias(x) is the identity leaf-relabel.
name: alias_id

law: detach(x) is the value identity — the autograd boundary the IR does not model (Inductor strips it in inference).
name: detach_id

law: detach_(x) — the in-place spelling of the same value identity.
name: detach_inplace_id

law: float(float(x)) = float(x) — dtype casts are idempotent.
name: float_idem

law: half(half(x)) = half(x) — dtype casts are idempotent.
name: half_idem

law: double(double(x)) = double(x) — dtype casts are idempotent.
name: double_idem

law: bfloat16(bfloat16(x)) = bfloat16(x) — dtype casts are idempotent.
name: bfloat16_idem

law: squeeze(unsqueeze(u, d), d) = u — the insert/remove pair cancels on the same normalized axis.
name: unsqueeze_squeeze

law: unsqueeze(squeeze(u, d), d) = u when u[d] == 1 — the remove/insert pair cancels on a size-1 axis only.
name: squeeze_unsqueeze

law: squeeze(u, d) on a non-1 axis removes nothing — a no-op the exporter's belt-and-braces squeezes leave behind.
name: squeeze_noop

law: reshape(u, shape(u)) = u — the no-op reshape strip (Inductor view-chain simplification).
name: reshape_noop

law: reshape(reshape(u, s0), s1) = reshape(u, s1) — view composition keeps only the final target.
name: reshape_reshape

law: broadcast_to(u, shape(u)) = u — the same no-op for the materializing spelling.
name: broadcast_to_noop

law: broadcast_to(u, s) = expand(u, s) — the strict spelling is a special case of the view.
name: broadcast_to_expand

law: slice(u, d, 0, e) = u when e >= u[d] — the full-cover slice strip (the export's ``x[..., :e]`` no-op).
name: slice_noop

law: The start-elided full-cover slice — ``x[..., :e]`` with e >= u[d].
name: slice_noop_nostart

law: index_select(u, d, range(u[d])) = u — the identity gather.
name: index_select_id

law: roll(u, shifts=0) = u — a zero shift on every axis.
name: roll_noop

law: pad(u, zeros) = u — an all-zero pad pad is a no-op.
name: pad_noop

law: repeat(u, ones) = u — tiling by 1 on every axis.
name: repeat_noop

law: permute(u, identity) = u.
name: permute_noop

law: permute(permute(u,P),Q) = permute(u, P∘Q) — permutation composition, minted as gather(P, Q).
name: permute_compose

law: movedim(movedim(u,s,d),d,s) = u — moving an axis forth and back is the identity.
name: movedim_involution

law: flatten(u, i, i) = u — a one-axis merge is a no-op.
name: flatten_noop

law: unflatten(u, d, (u[d],)) = u — a singleton split restores the same axis.
name: unflatten_noop

law: split(u, (u[d],), d, 0) = u — a one-section split is the whole tensor (the chunk_single sibling).
name: split_single

law: flip(flip(u, d), d) = u — reversing the same axes twice.
name: flip_involution

law: tril(tril(u, g), g) = tril(u, g) — masking is idempotent.
name: tril_idem

law: triu(triu(u, g), g) = triu(u, g).
name: triu_idem

law: clamp(clamp(u,l,h),l,h) = clamp(u,l,h) — same-bound nesting is a no-op.
name: clamp_idem

law: 1/(1+e⁻ˣ) folds to σ(x) — the manual-spelling fold (softmax_fold's sibling one kernel over).
name: sigmoid_fold

law: The div-spelled 1/(1+e⁻ˣ) folds to σ(x).
name: sigmoid_fold_div

law: 2σ(2x) − 1 folds to tanh(x).
name: tanh_fold

law: relu6(x+3)/6 folds to hardsigmoid(x).
name: hardsigmoid_fold

law: abs(abs(u)) = abs(u).
name: abs_idem

law: |u²| = u² — the square is already nonneg.
name: abs_square

law: (|u|)² = u² — abs is invisible to the square.
name: square_abs

law: √(u²) = |u| — the canonical spelling (NOT u — the negative branch keeps the abs).
name: sqrt_square

law: 1/√(u²) = 1/|u| — the rsqrt twin.

law: max(u, u) = u.
name: maximum_idem

law: min(u, u) = u.
name: minimum_idem

law: tanh is odd: tanh(−u) = −tanh(u).
name: tanh_neg

law: σ(−u) = 1 − σ(u) — the symmetric complement.
name: sigmoid_neg

law: softsign is odd.
name: softsign_neg

law: erf is odd.
name: erf_neg

law: sin is odd.
name: sin_neg

law: cos is even: cos(−u) = cos(u).
name: cos_neg

law: e⁻ᵘ = 1/eᵘ.
name: exp_neg_recip

law: log(eᵘ) = u — eᵘ > 0 always, so the inverse is total.

law: log(1/u) = −log(u).
name: log_recip

law: pow(u, 1) = u.
name: pow_one

law: pow(u, 0) = ones(u) — IEEE-total including NaN bases (pow(nan,0)=1); spelled ones_like so the mint carries u's shape (the eval compare is shape-strict, not broadcast).

law: pow(u, −1) = 1/u — the reciprocal spelling.  The Const-operand corner is excluded: an int-typed base does int exponentiation (pow(2,−1) → 0), which the pattern language can't dtype-guard otherwise.

law: pow(u, 0.5) = sqrt(u) — the canonical square root.

law: sqrt(u) = u^0.5 — the pow spelling (bridge to the pow family).

law: 1/(1/u) = u — reciprocal involution.

law: 1/u = reciprocal(u) — the div-spelled reciprocal folds.

law: reciprocal(u) = 1/u — the div spelling.

law: a + (−b) = a − b — the refold (sub_to_add's inverse).

law: u+u = 2u — the strength reduction.

law: 2u = u+u — the sharing direction.

law: −c folds to the negated Const leaf.

law: (u·c1)·c2 = u·(c1c2) — the scalar-factor fold (Inductor const-fold).

law: (A@B).mT = B.mT @ A.mT — the output's last-two swap folds into per-operand transposes (the BLAS NT/TN flag read, batched).

law: matmul(x, W.mT) ≡ linear(x, W): F.linear IS the BLAS-NT call — W stays in (out, in) storage and no transpose materialises.
